reviewSummary: Compared all six edited or added Skills with their cited current principle bodies at commit 94370a51c5e856ceffb68afdc8a3b48fdfb813d9. Compared the three edited Skills with their prior text for material regressions.
Checked how the six Skills fit into the nine-Skill inventory, including the distinction between workflow design, risk-based review, registered task policies, and tooling evaluation.

Cross-checked the 21 audited changes against the supplied state and managed provenance. All 11 changed or added principles map to the stated outputs. The two facts and eight ideas retain their snapshot types and have no generated provenance. Both reports remain open and reviewedTree is null.

The OSS release and tooling evaluation Skills are supported by their cited principles. The release Skill leaves the choice of changelog host open, and the tooling Skill evaluates trigger retirement within its design scope.

workflow-trigger-scope resolved. Manual and scheduled runs share a workflow when their processing matches. Trigger-specific decisions stay at the entry point, and the upper-level workflow calls existing procedures and handles shared checks.

workflow-state-guardrails resolved. Existing artifacts supply progress, additional state is limited to what safe handoff requires, and existing approval boundaries govern when a waiting state is needed.

workflow-model-scope partially resolved. Task difficulty and required quality guide model selection, workflows specify capabilities, and the escalation record covers explicit selection and default inheritance. The record still omits the identity of an explicitly selected model.

workflow-policy-outcomes resolved. Policy defines prohibited outcomes, and dangerous operations use a common preflight path that checks the target, authority, and proposed operation. Publication controls still cover alternate paths.

simplify-design-selection-thresholds resolved. Abstraction waits for multiple concrete uses. Persistence uses the smallest approach that meets current guarantees, stays replaceable behind its boundary, and keeps the Core separate from viewer and editor clients.

document-reference-scope resolved. The link-based rule applies to operational directives in AGENTS.md and SKILL.md. Each rule has one authoritative location, and material is split when that reduces lookup and editing effort.
task-policy-split-guardrail resolved. Step 2 retains the one-policy cap and explicitly preserves coherent tasks when policy applicability is the only reason to split them.
Carried forward the unaffected first-review coverage for the nine-Skill inventory, the OSS release and tooling evaluation Skills, and the provenance and report state for all 21 audited changes.

workflow-model-scope is resolved in skills/design-agent-workflows/SKILL.md. The revised text requires recording the selected model by name and the reason for choosing it. When explicit selection is unavailable, it requires recording that the default was inherited and why. Both cases match the supplied fixed-commit principle k-f1b6da308d1daaf7.
All other prior review coverage and source references carry forward.
limitations: The final re-review used only the supplied artifacts. Digest verification, change scope, and the passing state and Markdown checks rely on the parent’s evidence.
Runtime CI and publication remain pending.
evidence: Full content and source review followed by two scoped re-reviews: 01a1b82f-a63b-76d3-95b4-e80cacb6fb72, 01a1b833-5f62-79e3-9e3d-3100a7a46d39, 01a1b834-e40c-7b02-b679-f2b45b733a88. Seven required findings resolved on the final digest. Fixed 104-entry manifest and all 21 changes verified.
